Sourdough Pizza Dough

Use starter instead of yeast and give the balls a long, cool rise. Let them warm up before you stretch. Each ball starts at 270 g. Change the count before a long ferment so every piece is weighed from the start.

Detailed method

Sourdough pizzas. Currently 561 g flour, 70% hydration, 20% starter, 2.5% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 392.7 g water, 112.2 g starter, and 14 g salt, 1080 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 72.7% effective hydration. Currently 4 pizzas of 270 g each. No added yeast. Sauce, cheese, and other toppings are extra and are not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 112.2 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total.
  2. Mix Stir 561 g flour, 392.7 g water, the 112.2 g starter, and 14 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 70% the dough is soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover the dough in one piece at about 24°C (75°F) for about 60 minutes and fold it once. With 20% starter it only grows a little. Divide it before the cold rest.
  4. Divide Divide the 1080 g into 4 pieces of 270 g each, tighten each piece into a ball, and cover them. The default 1080 g uses a baking stone or tray about 40 cm across. If you change the amount, use a stone sized to fit, or bake in batches.
  5. Cold Refrigerate the covered balls at about 4°C (39°F) for 24 to 48 hours. They should spread a little and smell mild, not sharp.
  6. Warm Take the balls out 60 to 90 minutes before baking. Then stretch each ball by hand on a floured peel. Leave a rim and a thin center.
  7. Bake Heat the oven to 250°C (480°F) with a stone or steel for 45 minutes. Add sauce and cheese if you want them. Those toppings are extra and are not in the gram total. Bake 7 to 10 minutes, until the rim is spotted and the center is set. Rest 2 minutes before you cut.
